hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Sedimentation velocity analysis found a larger multi-oligomer-region occupancy for apoE4-(72-166), 59%, than for apoE3-(72-166), 55%, in PBS.
rows.Finding quote: The second major species was a broad peak at s = 3.5 to 6.5, with a total occupancy of 46 % for apoE2-(72-166), 55 % for apoE3-(72-166), and 59 % for apoE4-(72-166). This region may be the result of a contribution by multi-oligomers.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (higher occupancy of the multi-oligomer region in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments expressed in E. coli; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3, at 20°C; sedimentation velocity at 42,000 rpm and continuous c(s) analysis.

rows.Finding description: In PBS, apoE4-(72-166) formed a smaller intermediate oligomer than apoE3-(72-166), 51 versus 68 kDa, interpreted as tetramer versus hexamer, but its fitted local concentrations were higher: 0.18 versus 0.16 A280 in velocity and 0.05 versus 0.04 A280 in equilibrium.
rows.Finding quote: In the aqueous PBS solution, apoE-(72-166) peptides showed a major species of dimer, tetramer (for apoE4-(72-166)) or hexamer (for apoE2- and apoE3-(72-166)), and large aggregates, respectively, which indicated a significant polymerization.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (lower intermediate-oligomer mass but higher fitted intermediate-species signals in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, at 20°C; combined sedimentation velocity and multi-speed sedimentation equilibrium fitted with a three-discrete-species model.

rows.Finding description: In PBS, the large-aggregate species had higher fitted local concentrations for apoE4-(72-166) than apoE3-(72-166), 0.05 versus 0.03 A280 in velocity and 0.12 versus 0.06 A280 in equilibrium, although its fitted mass was lower, 210 versus 251 kDa.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (higher fitted large-aggregate signals but lower aggregate mass in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, at 20°C; global three-discrete-species analysis of sedimentation velocity and multi-speed sedimentation equilibrium.

rows.Finding description: Sedimentation velocity analysis of recombinant human apoE-(72-166) fragments in PBS found that the small species near 2 S occupied 6% for apoE4 versus 23% for apoE3, consistent with greater redistribution of apoE4 into larger assemblies.
rows.Finding quote: The first of these showed a sedimentation coefficient distribution of 20 % for apoE2-(72-166) and 23 % for apoE3-(72-166) at s = 2.0, but only 6 % for the same species of apoE4-(72-166).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (lower small-species occupancy in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments expressed in E. coli; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3, at 20°C; sedimentation velocity at 42,000 rpm with SEDFIT continuous c(s) analysis; no cells or endo-lysosomes.

rows.Finding description: In 5 mM DHPC, apoE4-(72-166) had higher fitted large-aggregate signals than apoE3-(72-166), 0.04 versus 0.03 A280 in velocity and 0.19 versus 0.06 A280 in equilibrium, while fitted aggregate masses were 217 versus 232 kDa.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (higher fitted large-aggregate signals but lower aggregate mass in 5 mM DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 5 mM DHPC at 20°C; global three-discrete-species sedimentation velocity/equilibrium analysis.

rows.Finding description: In 100 mM DHPC, apoE3-(72-166) and apoE4-(72-166) both predominantly occupied a single species near 1.1 S, with no significant difference reported between their major-species patterns.
rows.Finding quote: Finally, whilst apoE2-(72-166) maintained a two species distribution (s = 1.1 and 2.0) in 100 mM DHPC, its apoE3 and apoE4 counterparts maintained a single major species at s = 1.1 (Figure 2D).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (no change in the reported single-major-species pattern in 100 mM DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3, with 100 mM DHPC at 20°C; sedimentation velocity and continuous c(s) analysis.

rows.Finding description: In PBS, the fitted dimer-sized species had lower sedimentation-velocity local concentration for apoE4-(72-166), 0.02 A280, than for apoE3-(72-166), 0.07 A280; both equilibrium concentrations were zero, and fitted masses were 24 and 18 kDa, respectively.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (lower fitted dimer-sized-species signal in PBS sedimentation velocity)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, at 20°C; global SEDPHAT discrete-species fitting of sedimentation velocity at 42,000 rpm and equilibrium at 10,000, 15,000, and 20,000 rpm, each equilibrium speed for 18 hours.

rows.Finding description: In 5 mM DHPC, the dimer-sized species had lower fitted local concentrations for apoE4-(72-166) than apoE3-(72-166), 0.01 versus 0.08 A280 in velocity and 0 versus 0.08 A280 in equilibrium, with fitted masses of 22 versus 21 kDa.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (lower fitted dimer-sized-species signals in 5 mM DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 5 mM submicellar DHPC at 20°C; global three-discrete-species analysis of sedimentation velocity and equilibrium.

rows.Finding description: In 5 mM DHPC, apoE4-(72-166) and apoE3-(72-166) had similarly sized intermediate oligomers, 51 versus 52 kDa, while apoE4 had higher fitted local concentrations, 0.17 versus 0.15 A280 in velocity and 0.07 versus 0 A280 in equilibrium.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (higher fitted intermediate-oligomer signals in 5 mM DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 5 mM DHPC at 20°C; combined sedimentation velocity and equilibrium fitted to three discrete species.

rows.Finding description: In 50 mM DHPC, the larger peptide-lipid species had greater fitted mass for apoE4-(72-166) than apoE3-(72-166), 45 versus 40 kDa, and higher velocity concentration, 0.03 versus 0.02 A280, but lower equilibrium concentration, 0.14 versus 0.15 A280.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (higher larger-complex mass with discordant fitted concentration changes in 50 mM DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 50 mM DHPC at 20°C; global two-discrete-species sedimentation analysis; larger complexes interpreted as peptide dimers associated with micelles.

rows.Finding description: In 100 mM DHPC, the larger apoE4-(72-166)-lipid species had greater fitted mass than the apoE3 counterpart, 58 versus 50 kDa, and higher local concentrations, 0.01 versus 0 A280 in velocity and 0.11 versus 0.10 A280 in equilibrium.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (higher fitted larger-complex mass and signals in 100 mM DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 100 mM DHPC at 20°C; global two-discrete-species sedimentation velocity/equilibrium analysis; mass includes lipid, so peptide stoichiometry is uncertain.

rows.Finding description: In 50 mM DHPC, the small peptide-micelle species had a lower fitted velocity concentration for apoE4-(72-166), 0.29 A280, than apoE3-(72-166), 0.34 A280; equilibrium concentrations were both zero and fitted masses were 19 versus 20 kDa.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (lower fitted small-complex velocity signal in 50 mM DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 50 mM DHPC micelles at 20°C; two-discrete-species global sedimentation analysis; fitted masses include lipid.

rows.Finding description: In 100 mM DHPC, apoE4-(72-166) had lower fitted small-complex concentrations than apoE3-(72-166), 0.27 versus 0.32 A280 in velocity and 0.04 versus 0.08 A280 in equilibrium, with fitted masses of 20 versus 19 kDa.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (lower fitted monomer-micelle-complex signals in 100 mM DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 100 mM DHPC at 20°C; combined sedimentation velocity/equilibrium two-discrete-species fitting; masses include micellar lipid.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Lysosomal FITC–dextran/Texas Red–dextran ratios showed no significant difference in lysosomal pH between APOE4 and APOE3 neurons across three plates with two wells per genotype per plate.
rows.Finding quote: Our results show that endolysosomal pH is not changed in any of the APOE isoform-expressing cortical neurons (Fig. 3C,D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in lysosomal pH in human cortical neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); donor age and AD status were not stated. Cells received pH-sensitive FITC–dextran and pH-insensitive Texas Red–dextran for 24 hours, followed by a 24-hour chase; vesicular fluorescence ratios measured by Operetta imaging.

rows.Finding description: After bafilomycin A1, APOE4 neurons had fewer calcium sparks than APOE3 neurons, with printed means of 1.16±0.03 versus 1.71±0.03 sparks/min, in six replicates per genotype.
rows.Finding quote: Results demonstrate that APOE ε3, APOE ε2 and APOE−/− neurons had an average of 1.71±0.03, 1.63±0.03 and 1.49±0.04 spontaneous Ca2+ sparks/min, respectively (mean±s.e.m.). In contrast, APOE ε4 neurons had a significantly lower number of spontaneous Ca2+ sparks/min (1.16±0.03, P<0.0001) (Fig. 4A,B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower TRPML1-associated lysosomal calcium-release frequency)
rows.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); donor age and AD status were not stated. Fura2-AM imaging with 5 µM xestospongin C to inhibit ER IP3 receptors, followed by 200 nM bafilomycin A1; sparks counted for 5 minutes. The legend assigns untreated APOE3 n=6, 90 traces, and APOE4 n=6, 101 traces.

rows.Finding description: GPN-induced calcium-release traces indicated higher lysosomal calcium content in APOE4 than APOE3 human iPSC-derived cortical neurons.
rows.Finding quote: Using this experimental paradigm, we found that neurons expressing APOE ε4, the greatest genetic risk factor for LOAD, had significantly higher levels of lysosomal Ca2+ compared with APOE ε3 (P=0.0102), APOE ε2 (P<0.0001) and APOE−/− (P<0.0001) neurons (Fig. 3A).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosomal calcium content in human cortical neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons differentiated from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); neuronal differentiation involved 7 days in SynaptoJuice A followed by up to 2 weeks in SynaptoJuice B; donor age and AD status were not stated. Fura2-AM imaging after 2 µM ionomycin followed by 500 µM GPN.

rows.Finding description: In situ lysosomal calcium measurements showed no significant difference between APOE4 and APOE3 neurons, despite an upward trend in APOE4, using five biological replicates.
rows.Finding quote: Although not significant compared with APOE ε3 and APOE ε2, the trend seen in these data further confirms that lysosomal Ca2+ is indeed elevated in APOE ε4-expressing iPSC neurons (P=0.0116 versus APOE−/−).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in lysosomal calcium content by the in situ assay)
rows.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); donor age and AD status were not stated. In situ endolysosomal calcium estimated from calcium-sensitive OGB (0.5 mg/ml) relative to calcium-insensitive Texas Red–dextran (0.1 mg/ml); five biological replicates and one technical replicate per isoform.

rows.Finding description: ML-SA1-induced whole-cell calcium release showed no significant difference between APOE4 and APOE3 neurons in three biological replicates, although APOE4 showed an upward trend.
rows.Finding quote: The ML-SA1-induced Ca2+ release was not significantly different when comparing APOE isoforms, although there was a trend towards increased Ca2+ release in the APOE ε4 cortical neurons (Fig. 4C).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in whole-cell calcium release induced by ML-SA1)
rows.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); donor age and AD status were not stated. Fura2-AM imaging after 10 µM ML-SA1 without ionomycin or xestospongin pretreatment; the response includes calcium release from compartments beyond lysosomes. Three biological replicates and one technical replicate per isoform.

rows.Finding description: BODIPY-pepstatin-positive spot number showed no significant difference across APOE genotypes, including APOE4 versus APOE3, despite a trend toward fewer spots in APOE4 neurons.
rows.Finding quote: There was also a trend towards fewer BODIPY–pepstatin fluorescent spots per cell in the APOE ε4 neurons, but this was not significant (Fig. S2I).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in active-cathepsin-D-positive spot number)
rows.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); donor age and AD status were not stated. BODIPY-pepstatin labeling at 1:500 for 15 minutes at 37°C followed by Operetta spot counting; supplementary legend describes spots normalized to cell area. Three biological replicates with one technical repeat.

rows.Finding description: Mean FluoZin-3-AM spot intensity showed no significant difference between APOE4 and APOE3 neurons in three biological replicates.
rows.Finding quote: Our results show that there were no significant differences in Zn2+ levels between the cortical neurons expressing the different APOE isoforms (Fig. S2A–E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in zinc-probe mean spot intensity)
rows.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); donor age and AD status were not stated. FluoZin-3-AM loading at 5 µM for 30 minutes at 37°C followed by imaging and mean spot-intensity measurement; three biological replicates with one technical repeat.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Under fed conditions, APOE4-expressing human T98G cells contained approximately 20% more sarcosyl-insoluble aggregate protein than APOE3-expressing cells.
rows.Finding quote: In control conditions (“Fed”), T98G-apoE4 cells had ~20% higher levels of sarcosyl-insoluble intracellular aggregates than T98G-apoE3 cells (Fig. 2A and 2B, E3 vs. E4) in two different sets of clones.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher insoluble aggregate abundance, a surrogate of impaired protein clearance)
rows.Experimental system: Human T98G astroglioma/glioblastoma cells obtained from ATCC and stably expressing apoE3 or apoE4; two sets of clones reported. Fed cells received DMEM with 10% FBS for 3 hours at 37°C. Sarcosyl-insoluble proteins were recovered by ultracentrifugation, separated by SDS-PAGE, and stained with SYPRO Ruby. Lipid metabolism and autophagic flux were not measured.
rows.Data location: Fig. 2B, densitometry of the gels illustrated in Fig. 2A

rows.Finding description: Starvation decreased mitochondrial-protein abundance in APOE3-cell insoluble aggregates but increased it in APOE4-cell aggregates, suggesting an isoform-dependent defect in cargo clearance.
rows.Finding quote: Furthermore, apoE3 cells decreased these protein concentrations under starvation stress, but apoE4 cells paradoxically elevated these concentrations.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4 during starvation) -> (mitochondrial aggregate proteins increase rather than decrease)
rows.Experimental system: Human ATCC T98G astroglioma cells stably expressing apoE3 or apoE4; fed DMEM/10% FBS versus EBSS starvation for 3 hours at 37°C; proteomic analysis of sarcosyl-insoluble aggregates by LC-MS/MASCOT. Cargo abundance is an indirect mitophagy/lysosomal-clearance readout.

rows.Finding description: Proteomics found mitochondrial proteins enriched in sarcosyl-insoluble aggregates from APOE4-expressing T98G cells relative to APOE3-expressing cells, indirectly suggesting deficient lysosomal clearance.
rows.Finding quote: Consistent with deficient autophagy in apoE4-expressing cells, we find that these mitochondrial proteins are enriched in the apoE4 lysates compared to apoE3 lysates.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher mitochondrial-protein abundance in insoluble aggregates, a surrogate of impaired mitophagic clearance)
rows.Experimental system: Human ATCC T98G astroglioma cells stably expressing apoE3 or apoE4; sarcosyl-insoluble aggregate proteins separated by SDS-PAGE, trypsin-digested, analyzed by LC-MS, and identified using MASCOT. Mitochondrial cargo abundance was interpreted as a lysosomal/mitophagy surrogate; flux and lipid metabolism were not measured.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Recombinant full-length apoE3 and apoE4 (5 µg/ml) analysed by Superdex 200 gel filtration at neutral pH both existed as monomer and tetramer, but apoE4 was more monomeric, i.e. self-associated less than apoE3. This is the opposite direction to increased apoE4 aggregation. n = at least 3 independent experiments with different protein batches.
rows.Finding quote: The data in Figure 6A demonstrate that full-length apoE3 and apoE4 exist as both monomeric and tetrameric forms, but the monomer-tetramer distribution is different for the two isoforms, with apoE4 being more monomeric.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower self-association / tetramerization of lipid-free apoE in solution)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 (full-length), 14C trace-labeled, 5 µg/ml in Tris buffer pH 7.4; gel filtration on Superdex 200 (FPLC), cell-free

rows.Finding description: After deletion of residues 273-299, apoE4(1-272) eluted entirely as monomer, whereas apoE3(1-272) was still substantially tetrameric. ApoE4 self-associated less than apoE3 here too. n = at least 3 independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: Removal of residues 273–299 favors the monomeric state over the tetrameric state for both isoforms; apoE4 (1–272) exists completely as a monomer ( 27 ) whereas apoE3 (1–272) is significantly tetramerized ( Figure 6B ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3(1-272) -> APOE4(1-272)) -> (lower tetramerization; apoE4 fully monomeric)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human C-terminally truncated apoE3(1-272) and apoE4(1-272), 14C trace-labeled, 5 µg/ml, Tris buffer pH 7.4; Superdex 200 gel filtration, cell-free

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: In six independent mouse-astrocyte experiments, human E4 showed higher intracellular C+C intermolecular FRET than E3, supporting increased apoE–apoE proximity without establishing aggregate burden or endo-lysosomal localization.
rows.Finding quote: When comparing the interactions between corresponding combinations of the apoE termini, intermolecular FRET was higher for E4 and lower for E2, with E3 adopting intermediate FRET levels.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher intracellular C+C intermolecular FRET in mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Primary immortalized mouse astrocytes genetically null for endogenous apoE, transiently co-transfected with human apoE-RFP and apoE-GFP of the same isoform, E3 or E4, at a 1:1 ratio, 0.48 μg/cm2 each; collected 36 h after transfection, fixed in 2% PFA for 10 min, and analyzed by flow-cytometry FRET. Mouse strain and donor age not specified in supplied text; no endo-lysosomal localization.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Sequential extraction of hippocampi from 2-, 4-, and 6-month-old male EFAD mice showed no significant difference between apoE4 and apoE3 in formic-acid-extracted insoluble apoE levels.
rows.Finding quote: However, the lower total apoE4 levels are reflected only in their significant reduction in the TBSX fraction, as the levels of apoE2, apoE3, and apoE4 are comparable in the TBS- and FA-extracted fractions.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in insoluble hippocampal apoE levels)
rows.Experimental system: Bulk hippocampal tissue from male human APOE3- or APOE4-targeted-replacement/5xFAD mice aged 2, 4, and 6 months. EFAD mice were generated from APOE-targeted-replacement mice on a C57/B6 background and 5xFAD mice on a mixed C57BL/6×SJL background. Tissue underwent sequential TBS, TBS containing 1% Triton X-100, and 70% formic acid extraction; apoE was measured by ELISA. The formic-acid fraction operationally measures insoluble apoE without identifying aggregates or their subcellular location.
rows.Data location: Fig 5A, formic-acid extraction fraction; Discussion paragraph beginning “In E4FAD mice, total apoE levels in the brain are lower”

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Densitometry of western blots of RIPA brain homogenates showed significantly more low-molecular-weight (7-10 kDa) ApoE C-terminal fragments, which partition into the detergent-insoluble fraction, in AD APOE4/4 than AD APOE3/3 brains; this is fragmentation/insolubility in aged AD tissue, not endo-lysosomal aggregation in non-AD cells.
rows.Finding quote: We also measured an increase in LMW (7–10 kDa) fragments in the case of AD, the presence of APOEε4 further amplifies the effect.
rows.Finding summary: AD APOE4/4 brains had more 7–10 kDa ApoE fragments than AD APOE3/3 brains. Separate blots identified these fragments as primarily C-terminal and recovered most in the SDS extract after Triton extraction.
rows.Experimental system: Postmortem human temporal cortex gray matter from AD patients homozygous APOE3/3 or APOE4/4 (MADRC brain bank), RIPA homogenate, western blot with goat polyclonal anti-ApoE, densitometry over 3 blots

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Mass-spectrometry levels of ApoE in the detergent-insoluble (urea-soluble), high-molecular-weight amygdala fraction were stratified by APOE e4 status. A subset of e4 carriers had high insoluble ApoE. Insoluble ApoE was also enriched in dementia cases lacking e4. This is aged, mostly dementia/AD tissue, and the paper does not measure endo-lysosomal localization.
rows.Finding quote: Stratification according to the APOE ε4 status suggested that the presence of ε4 allele(s) led to high levels of insoluble ApoE in a subset of patients ( Figure 2 ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher detergent-insoluble high-MW ApoE in a subset of amygdalae)
rows.Experimental system: Postmortem human amygdala, University of Kentucky ADRC autopsy cohort (aged 62-100 y; cognitively normal, MCI, dementia); sequential detergent fractionation; urea-soluble fraction >171 kDa gel region; LC-ESI-MS/MS, MASCOT score

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: In the APOE3-parental isogenic human iPSC-derived astrocyte pair, APOE4 astrocytes showed a trend toward fewer lysosomes than APOE3 astrocytes, providing an abundance surrogate without establishing impaired acidification, degradation, or lipid metabolism.
rows.Finding quote: APOE4 astrocytes also exhibited a trend towards lower late endosomal and lysosomal number when compared to APOE3 astrocytes in both isogenic pairs (Figures S2C–F).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (trend toward fewer lysosomes in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from the isogenic pair generated from an APOE3-homozygous parental line; APOE3 versus APOE4 homozygotes. The two parental lines used in the study were Coriell AG09173 and AG10788, both female, but their genotype-to-line mapping is not supplied. Early-passage astrocytes, fewer than eight passages. The methods describe LysoTracker Red staining at 50 nM for 30 minutes at 37°C, followed by fixation and confocal imaging; the supplementary panel-specific assay description is unavailable. Donor age and Alzheimer’s disease status are not stated.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig S2C–F, cited collectively for late-endosome and lysosome numbers; exact lysosome-panel allocation unavailable.
